outcome: Obstetrical complications (premature contractions, gestational diabetes mellitus, preeclamptic toxemia, 2nd/3rd trimester bleeding or chorioamnionitis)
Rate of vaginal birth after cesarean delivery (VBAC)
cohort: 46 physicians and 116 nurses employed at one medical center who gave birth in its maternity hospital, compared to 162 women from the general population who gave birth during the same period in the same hospital.
finding: Medical personnel utilized ART more frequently and had more pregnancy complications as well as a lower incidence of VBAC than non-personnel, but neonatal outcomes were similar for both groups.
mod_finding: The rate of vaginal birth after cesarean delivery (VBAC) was lower in the study group (medical personnel) (22.2% vs. 33.3% for controls, P=0.03).
